title: Edge shadow wafermap lab notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory scratchpad for the "edge-shadow" wafermap runs (small fleet of edge nodes stubbed into staging) to surface latency islands and coldcache behavior across slices. Goal is to get hypothesis-driven artifacts: (1) map of p99 vs time-of-day for node subsets, (2) correlation with KV-cache hit and model-switch frequency, (3) candidate mitigations to test (prefix priming, prewarm windows, tiny batch gating).

Environment/setup:
- Model: trimmed-llama-v2-7b (quantized int8 runtime build: rdx-2025q4-int8)
- Serving binary: rdx-serving 1.14.2-edge (local debug build with extra hist logging)
- Fleet: 18 edge nodes (g4dn-equivalent vCPU/GPU), "shadow" traffic mirrored from hosted prod at 0.6x real QPS
- Request mix: 65% single-turn text-gen (avg tokens 120), 35% chat-like multi-turn (avg tokens 280)
- Arrival distribution: bursty daytime (zipf-ish), small nano-bursts at night
- Cache: KV prefix cache enabled on runtime; TTL 120s; cache-size per-node 400k entries (experimental)
- Rollout variant: 6 nodes with default batching config, 6 nodes with reduced max_batch_latency (8ms -> 3ms), 6 nodes with prefix-priming enabled (warmup RPC priming)

Quick commands used (staging):
- Start tracing: ./rdxctl trace start --scope=edge-shadow --out=trace-20260118.log
- Run replay: ./replayer --traffic=mirror-20260117.ndjson --scale=0.6 --target-tag=edge-shadow
- Extract tail: jq -r '.events[] | select(.latency_ms>2000) | .payload' replay-out.json | head -n 40 > tails-sample.json

Raw aggregated numbers (overall, shadow fleet):
- avg QPS seen: 155rps (scaled)
- p50 latency: 38 ms
- p95 latency: 160 ms
- p99 latency: 930 ms
- p999 latency (sampled): 2400+ ms (heavy tails aligned with microbatching spikes and context warmups)

Wafermap snapshot (node buckets by p99, 2026-01-18 09:00–12:00 window) - ASCII map (rows = node groups of 3, values = p99 ms):
[ groupA ][ groupB ][ groupC ][ groupD ][ groupE ][ groupF ]
[ 110   ][ 420   ][ 95    ][ 180   ][ 760   ][ 130   ]
[ 130   ][ 410   ][ 100   ][ 200   ][ 700   ][ 120   ]
[ 125   ][ 438   ][ 98    ][ 195   ][ 790   ][ 140   ]

Interpretation notes:
- GroupE is a clear outlier (p99 ~700–790ms). These nodes also show higher model-switch frequency (we observed fallbacks from trimmed-llama->trimmed-7b-approx on 30% of requests due to transient memory pressure).
- GroupB shows intermittent spikes around 400–440ms correlated with KV-cache misses (cache hit-rate ~42% during spikes vs baseline ~78%).
- GroupA/C/F are healthy baselines (p99 < 150ms) and have the highest steady cache-hit rates.

Sample log excerpt (tail sample):
[2026-01-18T09:22:13.987Z] req=abc123 node=groupE-02 stage=kvcache lookup=false latency_ms=1187 model_switch=true evicted_kv=23 mem_high=true
[2026-01-18T09:22:14.102Z] req=abc128 node=groupE-02 stage=runtime batch_wait_ms=26 inference_ms=520 total_ms=1603

Hypotheses emerging:
1) Edge nodes with smaller effective working set (due to more active fallback variants) are thrashing the local KV cache leading to large cold misses and heavy inference latency.
2) Model-switching costs are higher on edge (I/O+warmup) — the runtime currently does a full remap on variant change which triggers KV invalidation in some configurations.
3) Reduced max_batch_latency (3ms) reduces tail for small requests but increases overall GPU kernel churn causing slightly worse p95 for long-context chat requests (observed +12% p95).

Quick micro-experiments and results:
- Run A: turn on prefix-priming on all nodes (prewarm rpc to load KV for top-10 prefixes). Result: groupE p99 drops 700->240ms in the 30m window post-change. Cache hit-rate jumps from 46%->82%.
- Run B: enforce model pinning for 60s (no model-switch on fallback). Result: p99 groupE improves further to ~180ms, but error-rate for capacity-overshoot (~5xx) went up in some rare cases.
- Run C: reduce batch window to 3ms on healthy nodes only. Result: p50 improved by ~5ms, p95 worse by ~12% for long requests (confirming tradeoff).

Small CSV of run A (before/after prefixes) - columns: node, p95_before, p95_after, p99_before, p99_after, cache_hit_before, cache_hit_after
node-01,160,88,760,240,46,82
node-07,150,82,700,210,50,79
node-04,95,90,110,100,78,84

Anomalies / open questions:
- Why does groupB show intermittent low cache-hit windows? Hypothesis: background eviction job runs every ~5–7m but it shouldn't affect buckets this much. Need to instrument eviction traces.
- Are the model-switches coming from routing policy (fallbacks) or from the runtime eviction? Look at routing logs for 2026-01-18 09:20–09:30.
- Disk vs RAM pressure: metrics show swap events on two groupE nodes around spikes — is the telemetry misreporting or are we actually OOMing and swapping? (cc: infra team)

Next steps / experiment plan (short):
- 01: Instrument eviction traces (rdxctl evict-trace start) across groupB/E for 24h.
- 02: Roll prefix-priming to more nodes for 12h A/B (already promising). Add dashboard tile for priming effectiveness.
- 03: Create reproducible micro-replay that forces model-switch (script attached) and run under profiler (nvprof) on a spare node to measure exact warmup cost in ms.
- 04: Add feature flag to avoid KV invalidation on soft model-switches (proposal draft).

Notes to self / quick TODOs:
- Upload tails-sample.json to shared index (s3://rdx-shadow/tails/edge-v1/20260118/).
- Open a Linear task for eviction-instrumentation: RED-3576 (tag infra + runtime).
- Keep the prefix-priming patch as a runtime flag (not default) until we validate that it doesn't amplify memory churn.

Conclusions (early):
- Prefix priming + short model pin windows seem to be the fastest path to reduce p99 islands on the shadow edge fleet.
- There are tradeoffs: prewarm increases memory working set and can amplify rare 5xxs when capacity is tight. We need robust canary and mem-pressure alarms.

Rough decision suggestion for next meeting (runtime owners):
- Ship prefix-priming as opt-in canary to Dedicated/Edge customers and measure for 2 weeks. Pair with eviction-instrumentation and a mem-pressure kill-switch.

End of note. Will iterate after eviction traces come back.

-- Claudie
